title: Sec Eng Handover Labs sync — 2026-08-25
content:
Meeting: Security Engineering handover / labs sync
Date: 2026-08-25 10:30-11:15 PT
Location: Zoom / in-person (SF)
Attendees: Priya (owner), Alex, Maya, Samir, Lena + FYI: JT (SRE)

Objective: quick triage roll-up, coordinate secrets remediation work, agree threat-model checkpoints for Private v2 kickoff. Short, action-driven.

1) Current triage snapshot (quick counts)
- Total open security tickets: 28 (was 31 last week)
- P0/P1 (blocking/exploit-in-wild): 1 (SEC-1423)
- P2: 6
- P3: 21
- Secrets incidents (new this week): 2 (one expired token, one leaked to CI logs)
- Threat-modeling in-progress: Private v2 (owner: Maya), Edge routing changes (owner: Samir)

2) Deep-dive: SEC-1423 (ramp-worker privilege escalation) — current status
- Summary: internal discovery by red-team automation flagged a path where user-supplied model configs could trigger an unchecked exec path in ramp-worker, allowing container escape into node-level process namespace under specific kernel versions. Repro steps in JIRA.
- Risk: high (CAPEX: potential data exfil via local fs mounts if exploited). Affects Dedicated and Private if customers use early-access config flags.
- Root cause hypothesis: insufficient validation of config templates + race in temp-file handling during model load.
- Mitigation applied: hotfix v2.1.3 to ramp-worker that adds strict template schema validation + atomic tempfile creation. Deployed to canary pool (us-west-2-dedicated-canary) at 2026-08-25 06:00 PT.
- Validation: smoke tests + e2e harness show no repro on canary. JT ran kernel compatibility checks; affected kernels flagged and nodes cordoned.
- Next steps / owners:
  - Rollout plan: Alex to execute canary -> gradual rollout to dedicated pools (target: 2026-08-26 14:00 PT) (JIRA: SEC-1423-R01).
  - Customer comms: Samir to draft ops-notice for impacted Dedicated customers by EOD 2026-08-25. Use template in CONFLUENCE:sec/incident-comms.
  - Postmortem: Priya to lead incident timeline and RCA write-up (target draft 2026-08-28).

Notes / decisions: prefer in-place hotfix + config validation vs immediate rollback. We will keep fallback model-variant routing active for any customers on private networks until full rollout confirmed.

3) Secrets workstream (SEC-1478 and related)
- Finding A: kubernetes service-account token leaked in CI logs for internal repo (short-lived token issued by automation). Token TTL was 24h but was committed in logs persisted in artifact storage.
- Action taken: token revoked immediately (Maya), artifact retention rule tightened (infra PR merged), and CI runner sanitized history (job log purge) where feasible.
- Finding B: credential parameterization gap in deploy scripts: some infra scripts still read plaintext from environment in ad-hoc jobs.
- Remediations:
  - Rotate all k8s sa tokens created by automation in last 72h (Maya, complete).
  - Add log scrubbing step to CI runners and ensure that any token-like pattern (>20 chars, base64-looking) is scrubbed before upload (Infra PR #482). Owner: Alex. ETA: 2026-08-27.
  - Expand secret scanning rules in pre-commit and CI (detect vault paths, JWTs, SSH private key headers). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-09-02.
- Longer-term: move automation to use short-lived ephemeral credentials via OIDC (GH Actions OIDC or GCP workload identity) for runner tasks. Investigate HSM-backed signing for sensitive ops. Owner: Lena (investigation ticket SEC-1502).

Notes to self: create an internal checklist for rotating leaked tokens (rotate -> revoke -> audit -> notify -> rotate dependent credentials). Keep checklist next to incident playbooks.

4) Threat modeling: Private v2 (initial checkpoint)
- Context: Private v2 introduces customer-managed routing proxies and optional on-prem agent that accepts model bundles. This expands attack surface at the network and packaging layer.
- Goals for this sprint: (a) identify trust boundaries, (b) enumerate bootstrap threats for agent, (c) propose hardening controls for artifact signature verification and agent update channel.
- Key risks called out in quick brainstorm:
  - Model bundle poisoning if signature verification missing or weak. (Mitigation: sigs + allowlist + timestamping)
  - Supply-chain risk via third-party build images; need SBOM requirement and CI validations.
  - Local privilege escalation from agent auto-updater on older OS/distro combos. (Mitigation: drop privileges, run as unprivileged user, use kernel feature checks)
- Action items:
  - Threat model workshop with Eng + Product + Legal scheduled 2026-08-31. Owner: Maya. Scope doc: CONFLUENCE:sec/private-deploy-threatmodel (please add pre-read).
  - Temporary gating: require signed bundles for any private agent install on customer-managed hosts. Owner: Product (ask: PJ).
  - Add a CI policy that fails build if SBOM not attached for images that will run in Private. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-09-08.

5) Playbook / automations discussed
- Improved triage playbook draft: add specific decision tree for secrets leakage (revoke/rotate/audit/notify), escalate to P1 if token had >1 scope or long TTL. (Draft in CONFLUENCE:sec/playbooks/secret-rotation)
- Automated cordon + node-drain job for kernels with known vuln signatures. JT will own short script, keep as runbook first.
- Proposal: nightly security scan of canary clusters for config-shock (unexpected mountpoints, skip-capabilities). Owner: Alex. Prototype by 2026-09-01.

6) Open questions / blockers
- Do we require forced KMS rotations for Dedicated customers? Product input needed on billing impact. (Flagged to Product / PJ)
- How aggressive should we be with log retention truncation for CI artifacts? Legal wants 90-day retention for audit; security wants shorter for secrets safety. Need tradeoff decision. (Action: Priya to sync with Legal on 2026-08-26).
- Private v2 signing: who will operate the signing key for default bundles? (Options: Redwood-operated HSM vs customer bring-your-own signing.) Add to threat-model agenda.

7) Action items (consolidated)
- Alex: execute SEC-1423 rollout to dedicated pools (target 2026-08-26 14:00 PT). JIRA: SEC-1423-R01. (in-progress)
- Samir: draft and send customer ops-notice for affected Dedicated customers (EOD 2026-08-25). (in-progress)
- Maya: rotate/revoke tokens + schedule Threat-model workshop (done / scheduled 2026-08-31)
- Alex: merge infra PR for log-scrubbing and add CI step (PR #482). ETA 2026-08-27.
- Samir: add SBOM gating ticket (SEC-1508). ETA 2026-09-08.
- Priya: incident RCA draft (SEC-1423) by 2026-08-28 and legal sync on retention policy 2026-08-26.
- Lena: investigate OIDC/HSM options for ephemeral runner creds (SEC-1502). ETA 2026-09-10.

8) Meeting cadence / next check-in
- Weekly security sync remains Tuesdays 10:30 PT. For this incident we will do a checkpoint call Friday 2026-08-26 09:00 PT to confirm rollout and customer comms.

Quick notes (informal):
- "notes to self": ensure the incident template includes a field for kernel versions observed and the exact node image; saved a snippet into CONFLUENCE incident template.
- Keep the canary tag stable and ensure the rollback path is tested in a staging window before each rollout.

Attachments / reference: links under linked_artifacts above; see JIRA tasks for reproduction steps and test harness logs.

End of notes.
